_about: Batch B3a (Scheduler + KV cache manager). Owner: the B3a writer. Reused, not redefined: scheduler, token-budget, chunked-prefill, preemption, block-pool, kv-cache-group, prefix-caching (core); scheduler-output, output-placeholder, async-scheduling (t1); hash-chain (b1b); profile-run (b2b).

running-queue.short: The list Scheduler.running: the requests that hold KV blocks and take part in steps. The scheduler serves it first in each step, from the front.

waiting-queue.short: The queue of requests that are not running yet: new requests and preempted ones. Its order comes from the scheduling policy (FCFS deque or priority heap).

num-computed-tokens.short: The number of tokens of a request whose KV values are in the KV cache (or are computed by a step already started). The scheduler gives tokens until it catches up with num_tokens.
num-computed-tokens.long: Set to 0 by Request.__init__ ({{cite vllm/v1/request.py:184}}); advanced in _update_after_schedule ({{cite vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:1716}}); reset to 0 on preemption ({{cite vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:1680}}).

long-prefill-threshold.short: A cap on the tokens that one request can get in one step. 0 (the default) means no cap. The scheduler ignores it when only one request is running or waiting.
long-prefill-threshold.long: Field: {{cite vllm/config/scheduler.py:79-84}}; applied at {{cite vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:677-683}} and {{cite vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:764-765}}.

recompute-preemption.short: vLLM's only kind of preemption: the scheduler frees all KV blocks of the request and sets num_computed_tokens to 0. Later the request computes its tokens again (prefix caching can give some back).

scheduling-policy.short: How the scheduler orders waiting requests and picks a preemption victim: fcfs (default, arrival order) or priority (smaller priority value first, then arrival time).

kv-cache-block.short: The scheduler-side record of one KV cache block: block_id, ref_cnt, the block hash (only when full and cached) and two links for the free queue. The KV data itself is on the GPU.

free-block-queue.short: A doubly linked list of all free KV blocks in eviction order. The pool takes new blocks from the front. Freed blocks without a hash go to the front, cached blocks to the end.

null-block.short: Block 0 of the block pool. It is never given to a request. It fills block table places that hold no data, for example blocks outside a sliding window.
null-block.long: {{cite vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py:184-188}}; KV cache usage leaves it out ({{cite vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py:888-892}}).

allocate-slots.short: The KVCacheManager method that the scheduler calls for each scheduled request. It adds prefix-cache hits, gets new blocks for the new tokens, caches full blocks, or returns None when blocks are short.

block-table.short: For each request, the list of physical block ids that hold its KV values, in token order. The scheduler sends new block ids; Model Runner V2 keeps the table on the GPU.

kv-cache-usage.short: The fraction of KV blocks that requests hold now: 1 − free blocks / (all blocks − 1). Free cached prefix blocks count as free. Prometheus shows it as vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc (0 to 1).
